column2: req_desc

Station day dial
Show each site's local day as a dial of station rings whose booked, held and your-own segments come from the day endpoint for that site and date.

Placing a hold
Let a renter, or staff on a renter's behalf, place a hold on 15-minute boundaries for 15 minutes to 12 hours, validated as stated in API and Business rules.

One winner per contested slot
When several claims overlap the same station time at once, exactly one hold is created and every other claim is refused with the winning hold as its blocker.

Server-timed hold expiry
Holds expire on the server's clock with a published exclusive edge, free their time at that instant, and send one hold-expired email, as qualified in Business rules.

Letting a hold go
A renter can release their own live hold early, which frees the time immediately and sends no email.

Lost claim snaps back
When the server refuses a dragged claim, the arc retracts along its path, the competing time appears with its label, and the dial status explains why.

Distinguishable time states
Free, held, booked and your-own time differ on the dial by pattern and visible text label as well as colour, at the contrast stated in Visual design.

Claiming time on the dial
A renter sweeps an arc on a free ring, sees hours and price count live, and on release gets a held arc with a countdown and an open Checkout dialog.

Confirming with pack hours and card
Confirming a hold applies available pack hours first and records the card remainder and deposit in Kill Bill, as qualified in Business rules.

Pay now or pay later
A card balance can be paid at confirmation or later until the booking's unpaid cutoff, and a booking shows Paid only once Kill Bill records the time payment.

All-or-nothing confirmation
Confirmation either records the booking, its pack reservation, its Kill Bill payments and one queued email together, or changes nothing and undoes any partial charge.

Liability certificate gate
A booking cannot be confirmed unless the renter has a stored liability certificate valid on every local date the booking touches.

Booking confirmation email
Each successful confirmation sends exactly one email to the renter listing station, local start and end, hours and amounts for every booked date.

Checkout journey
A renter with a live hold buys a pack if needed, confirms in the Checkout dialog, and sees a Paid ticket on the rail and an updated pack balance.

Weekly repeating holds
A hold can repeat weekly for up to 12 weeks at the same local wall-clock times and is created for all weeks or none.

Wall-clock times across clock changes
Local times that do not exist or happen twice on clock-change days resolve by the single published rule in Business rules.

Billing actual elapsed hours
Bookings, quotes, tickets, invoices and emails count and bill the real elapsed minutes between start and end, including on clock-change days.

Clock-change days on the dial
The dial shows 23 hour ticks on the spring change day and 25 on the autumn change day, with the repeated hour labelled by zone.

Booking a recurring overnight shift
A renter holds and confirms a four-week Sunday 01:00–05:00 shift across the autumn change and sees the true hours on every ticket.

Buying an hour pack
A renter buys a 20-hour pack through Kill Bill exactly once per idempotency key, and the hours become available immediately.

Paired hour ledger
Every pack movement is two entries that sum to zero, and available, reserved and used hours always equal the sums of their entries.

Pack balance from the ledger
Every screen shows the server's available pack hours and refreshes them after each action that moves hours.

Check-in and check-out
Front desk checks a confirmed booking in within its window and checks it out later, which moves its reserved pack hours to used.

Overrun charged once
Front desk bills an overrun in minutes once per booking, and replaying the same request never charges again.

Cleaning fee and settlement
Front desk can add one cleaning fee after check-out and then settles the booking, which refunds its deposit in Kill Bill.

Booking state guard
Every booking action outside its legal state is refused with the transition error, and every state change writes one attributed audit event.

Running the counter
A front-desk lead books a walk-up renter, checks them in, charges an overrun, checks out, adds a cleaning fee and settles from the counter screen.

Scheduling a cancellation policy
A manager schedules a new cancellation notice period for a site from today or a later local date.

Refund terms fixed at booking
A cancellation is refunded or forfeited by the policy version in force when the booking was confirmed, never by a later one.

Booking's own terms on every surface
The booking detail, ticket, cancel dialog, invoice and confirmation email all quote the booking's own policy terms.

Cancellation replay safety
Replaying a cancellation with the same key returns the original result and refunds nothing twice.

Cancelling a booking
A renter opens a ticket, reads the refund outcome in the cancel dialog, confirms, and sees the cancelled ticket with its refund summary.

Unpaid balance cutoff
A booking whose card balance is still unpaid at its local cutoff is cancelled automatically, as qualified in Business rules.

Unpaid cancellation notice
Each automatic unpaid cancellation sends exactly one notice email to that booking's renter.

Daily station utilisation
The utilisation report and its CSV cover the site's local day of 23, 24 or 25 hours and count only booked station minutes.

Manager's morning report
A manager reads site totals, searches renters, opens and downloads utilisation, and schedules a policy change from the manage screen.

Document uploads checked by content
Renter documents are accepted only as PDF, PNG or JPEG judged by their bytes and within the published size limit.

Private document storage
Documents are stored in MinIO under server-chosen keys and served only to their renter and to staff of the renter's operator.

Expiry reminder once
Each document triggers exactly one reminder email starting 14 local days before it expires.

Keeping documents current
A renter refused for a missing certificate uploads one, sees it listed as current, and then confirms.

Inspector binder links
A manager creates a binder link for one site and date range that expires, can be revoked, and can be regenerated so that the old address stops working.

Binder contents
A binder lists each scheduled renter's bookings and daily document status for its site and range only, with no contact or payment data, and refuses every change.

Binder PDF
Each binder link has a generated PDF stored in MinIO and downloadable through the link.

Inspector visit
An inspector opens a binder link, reads the schedule and document status, and downloads the PDF without signing in.

Own records only
A renter can open only their own holds, bookings, invoices, ledger and documents, and any other identifier answers not found.

Operator isolation on derived surfaces
Search, totals, reports, exports, dial labels and binders never include another operator's sites, renters or bookings.

Manager override with reason
A manager can cancel a confirmed booking with a full refund or release a hold, giving a reason recorded with their name.

Booting with billing or mail down
The app starts and serves with Kill Bill or Mailpit unreachable at boot, answers the health check, and reports which service is delayed in its status and banner.

Billing outage leaves no trace
While Kill Bill is unreachable, every card action is refused with the billing error and changes nothing, while pack-only bookings still confirm.

Mail outage queues email
While Mailpit is unreachable, actions still succeed and each of their emails is counted once as queued instead of being lost.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from the run manifest on the stated port and answers the health check.

Sign-in and roles
Seeded users sign in with email and password, receive a session, and are limited to their role's actions and their scope.

One error shape and precedence
Every API error uses one JSON shape and follows one precedence order.

Responsive layout
The board, counter, manage, documents, pack and binder screens fit 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 with no page-level horizontal scroll.

Keyboard dial and reduced motion
The dial is fully operable by keyboard with announced states, and with reduced motion every animation becomes an instant change.

Motion timing
Dial snaps, spring-back, fill, retract, numeral tweens and ticket slides happen within the durations stated in Motion and effects.

Kitchen ticket-rail look
The screens read as an orderly order-ticket rail on warm paper, with a single tomato accent kept for live and claimed time.

Secrets stay on the server
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment on the server and never hard-coded or sent to the browser.

Server boundary
The server enforces body limits and same-origin writes, and never serves source, configuration or credentials.
/app/run.json is a JSON object with exactly the string keys _schema (value run-manifest-v1), install, build and serve.

/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree reported by npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) with name, version and licence, plus each bundled font and icon set.
Shipped packages, fonts and icons use only MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, BlueOak-1.0.0, CC0-1.0 or OFL-1.1 licences.
No datastore beyond the provided Postgres and MinIO is used: no SQLite, Redis, embedded database, or application state kept in local files.
The provided service definitions and their seeded credentials are left unchanged.
All application source is TypeScript compiled with strict enabled in tsconfig.json.
The browser loads every script, style, font and icon from the app's own origin, with no third-party CDN.
